This has reference to your letter dated 5 March 2018 seeking this Department's help on the Anti-Rider ordinances passed by Mandaluyong City, Taal, Batangas and Mandaue, Cebu. Allegedly, the ordinance were aimed to pass the accountability to the innocent by forcing the motorcycle riders (including you) to replace their helmets and prevent them from carrying passengers. Since this Department was not furnished with a copy of the assailed ordinances, we presumed that the same were validly passed by the sanggunian members. Foremost, we would like to inform you that duly approved ordinances are presumptively valid acts and thus enjoy the presumption Of regularity on the part Of the public concernedl. An ordinance that has undergone the procedural process for its enactment under the Local Government Code is presumed valid unless declared otherwise by our courts of justice2. Clearly, matters involving question on the validity or constitutionality of a duly enacted ordinance may stand on its own and therefore remain valid until judicially declared as null and void. Thus, judicial declaration of nullity of ordinance is an available remedya. Secondly, an action for declaratory relief' as a remedy may also be resorted to if adequate relief is not available through other existing forms of actions or proceedings. " DILG Legal Opinion No. 24, 52011 dated 14 June 2011 2 DILG Legal Opinion No. 5, S.2018 dated 25 January 2018 3 DOJ Opinion No. 87-2012 dated 18 September 2012 Declaratory relief is defined as an action by any person interested in a deed, will, contract or written instrument, executive order or resolution, to determine any question of construction or validity arising from the instrument, executive order or regulation, or statute; and for declaration of his rights and duties thereunder. The only issue that may be raised in such a petition is the question or validity of provisions in an instrument or statute (Province of Camarines Sur vs. CA. et.a/.. GR Nn 175/V,d

Nevertheless, for purposes of academic discussion, we are of the considered view that the subject ordinances are valid and reasonable as the same caters on the welfare and safety of the constituents of the LGU. In the landmark case of Magtajas vs. Pryce Properties5, the Supreme Court held that one of the substantive requirements of a valid ordinance is that it must not contravene the Constitution or any statute. Let it be noted that Section 6 of Republic Act (RA) NO. 10054, otherwise known as the "Motorcycle Helmet Act of 2009': provides that: 'Section 3. Mandatory Use of Motorcycle Helmets. - All motorcycle riders, including drivers and back riders, shall at all times wear standard protective motorcycle helmets while driving, whether long or short drives, in any type of road and high way. Standar rotective motor cle helm ts are a ro riate helmets for 177Qgorc.y@e riders that comply with the specifications issued by_ the Depprtment of Trade and Industry (DTI). (Emphasis given) The DTI shall issue guidelines, which should include the specifications regarding standard protective motorcycle helmets. " The said provision explicitly sets standard for protective helmets. In addition, the Land Transportation Office (LTO) issued Memorandum Circular on the Guidelines in the enforcement of violations relating to the mandatory wearing of standard protective motorcycle helmets by all motorcycle riders while riding6. With respect to preventing you from carrying passengers, Section 7 of RA No. 4136 or the "Land Transportation and traffic Code 't states that: 'Section 7. Registration Classification. - Everymotor vehicle shall be registered under one of the following described classifications: (a) private passenger automobiles; (b) private trucks; and (c) private motorcycles. scooters, or 117Qtor wheel attachments. drivers and back riders as mentioned in Memorandum Circular No. VPT-2012-1714, shall at all times wear standard protective motorcycle helmets while driving, whether long or short drives, in any type of road and highway. This Department was not furnished with a copy of the assailed ordinance, thus, with the presumption of regularity on the part of the public concerned, we believe that the prohibition to carry passengers in the subject ordinance applies only if the transport is with pay. Please be informed that LGUs hayethe power to pass ordinances provided that the same do not contravene the Constitution or any statute. Lastly, if these LGUs are in the process of passing ordinances, we recommend that you should provide them with your insights/views on the matter for their consideration. cc: LS:90 Thank you for your concern and we hope to have enlightened you on the matter.
